hints.content: The cruising speed on the flight from Philadelphia to Barcelona is $550\,\text{mph}$.  What is the cruising speed on the flight home?

Let's look at the chart.  After $\red1$ hour, the plane had flown $530$ miles, so the speed was $530\,\text{mph}$. The cruising speed is constant, but let's see what the other entries in the chart tell us.

After $\blue2$ hours, the plane traveled $1060$ miles, so the speed was 

$\dfrac{1060\,\text{miles}}{\blue2\, \text{hours}}=530\,\text{mph}$. 

After $\green3$ hours,  the plane traveled $1590$ miles, so the speed was 

$\dfrac{1590\,\text{miles}}{\green3\, \text{hours}}=530\,\text{mph}$. 

This is less than the cruising speed on the flight from Philadelphia to Barcelona.
**The cruising speed from Philadelphia to Barcelona is faster.**

question.content:
Diego is flying from Philadelphia to Barcelona.  On the trip to Barcelona, the plane flies at a constant cruising speed of $550\,\text{mph}$.

On the trip home, Diego makes a chart of the plane's progress once it reaches its cruising speed, which is constant.

**Which is faster, the cruising speed on the flight from Philadelphia to Barcelona, or the cruising speed on the flight home?**

||||
-:|-:|-:|-:
Hour|$1$|$2$|$3$
Miles|$530$|$1060$|$1590$

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.content: The cruising speed on the flight from Philadelphia to Barcelona
The cruising speed on the flight home
The two cruising speeds are the same.
